name: St Nicholas Fields Local Nature Reserve
short_description: Apple and pear trees on York's former landfill.
description: A 24-acre Local Nature Reserve in Tang Hall, managed by St Nicks. The northern area contains many self-seeded apple and pear trees grown from discarded household fruit cores — the fruit has been tested and confirmed safe to eat. Hawthorn, elder, hazel and blackthorn also produce abundant hedgerow harvests. Respectful foraging is explicitly welcomed by the site.

name: Fulford Community Orchard
short_description: 90-year-old orchard saved from development in Fulford.
description: Over fifty heritage trees — plums, damsons, pears and apples — survive from the original orchard belonging to the former Naburn Hospital. Saved from development and now a community orchard for Fulford residents. Volunteer sessions on the second Sunday of each month; windfalls and ripe fruit freely available.

name: Leeman Road Orchard (Edible York / Abundance)
short_description: Abundance York's urban harvest orchard near the railway.
description: Part of Edible York's Patchwork Orchard project planting 200 fruit trees across the city from 2012–13. The Leeman Road site is managed by Abundance York volunteers who harvest and distribute fruit to the community. Apple HQ equipment store is nearby on Salisbury Road.

name: Holgate Community Garden
short_description: Organic edible garden with espaliered apples and fruit trees.
description: A volunteer-run community garden established in 2014 at Holgate Allotments. Features six raised vegetable beds, a herb and currant bed, espaliered apple trees on a south-west-facing wall, raspberry canes, and eight young fruit trees including plum, gage and heritage apple varieties. Organically managed and open to the community.

name: Rowntree Park Orchard Area
short_description: Memorial park with developing orchard and wildlife area.
description: A 25-acre park on the River Ouse gifted to York by the Rowntree family in 1921. The Friends of Rowntree Park have developed a wildlife area at the rear of Butcher Terrace Field which includes an orchard being enhanced as part of a 4-year biodiversity project. Windfalls available from fruit trees in season.

name: Nether Poppleton Millennium Green Orchard
short_description: Thriving millennium orchard beside a wildlife pond.
description: One of two green spaces created in York to mark the Millennium. The site is managed by local people who have planted a thriving orchard. In addition to fruit trees the pond attracts cuckoos, reed buntings and corn buntings. Deer, foxes and bats can also be seen here.

name: Rawcliffe Bar Country Park Hedgerows
short_description: Blackberries and hedgerow fruit in north York's country park.
description: A large country park on reclaimed landfill north of York, managed by City of York Council. The woodland edges and hedgerows within the park carry good crops of blackberries, rosehips and hawthorn haws through late summer and autumn.

name: York City Walls Elderflower and Elder
short_description: Elder bushes flowering and fruiting along the medieval walls.
description: Elder bushes grow along the base and outer banks of York's medieval city walls. The flowers can be gathered in June for cordial and fritters; the berries ripen to a deep purple by September and are popular for elderberry syrup and wine. Access along the free-to-walk wall walk.

name: West Bank Park Wild Garlic and Hawthorn
short_description: Former Backhouse Nursery arboretum with spring wild garlic.
description: A 16-acre park in Holgate occupying the former site of the 19th-century Backhouse Nurseries, with a mature woodland and arboretum. Wild garlic carpets the shaded woodland floor in spring, and hawthorn and elder in the hedgerows provide hedgerow harvests in summer and autumn.

name: Museum Gardens Mulberry and Edible Trees
short_description: Ancient mulberry and fruit trees in the botanic gardens.
description: The Yorkshire Museum Gardens contain historic specimen trees including an ancient mulberry and various fruit trees within the botanic planting established in the 1830s. The gardens also feature an Edible Wood developed by York Art Gallery. Admission is free; foraging of windfalls is discreet and informal.

name: Leeman Road Millennium Green Wild Greens
short_description: Riverside green with planted trees and wild herbs.
description: One of York's largest public green spaces between the River Ouse and the railway line. Trees and wildflowers planted by the Leeman Road Millennium Green Trust. Garlic mustard (Jack-by-the-Hedge) and horseradish grow along sunny edges; the river bank supports watermint.

name: Strensall Common Bilberries and Blackberries
short_description: Heathland bilberries and woodland berry picking north of York.
description: A beautiful large heathland northeast of York with public footpaths. The open heathy areas carry bilberry plants fruiting in July and August; brambles at the woodland edges provide good blackberry picking from August into September.

name: Haxby Road Greenfields Community Garden
short_description: School and community orchard with fruit and vegetables.
description: A combined Haxby Road Primary School and community garden orchard started in 2011, designed by local residents and scouts. The community growing area features an orchard, fruit and vegetable beds, wildflower meadow and nature-friendly planting open for community harvest.

name: River Ouse Banks Wild Garlic and Rosehips
short_description: Ouse riverside wild garlic in spring and rosehips in autumn.
description: The wooded and scrubby river banks of the Ouse south of the city, accessible via the riverside footpath from Rowntree Park towards Bishopthorpe, support wild garlic in spring and hedgerow rosehips and sloes in autumn.

name: Tang Hall Beck Sweet Chestnuts and Hazelnuts
short_description: Woodland nut gathering beside Tang Hall Beck.
description: The tree canopy and scrubby woodland margins along Tang Hall Beck, close to St Nicks nature reserve, include hazel coppice producing hazelnuts in September and October. Sweet chestnut trees in the nearby Knavesmire parkland also provide autumn pickings.
